messages.author: Shiho Ohno
messages.body:
Dear Amber Administrator
Please excuse me for asking this question.
My name is Sasaki, Tohoku Medical and Pharmaceutical University.
I have a question about Amber, so I would like to contact you.
Q.I'm trying to install AmberTools19 on Amber18.
Initially, I found benchmarks, src, test, and README in the Amber18
directory, and saved AmberTools19.tar.bz2 in the Amber18 directory$B!!(B
similarly, and unzipped it using tar xvfj AmberTools19.tar.bz2.
As a result, a new amber18 directory is added in the amber18 directory
(there are dat, doc and test directories in the new amber18). Is this normal
behavior?
Q.Also, if I want to define an environment variable, should I do the export
AMBERHOME=... in a new Amber18 directory?
I would appreciate your answer.
Thank you very much for your time.
Tohoku Medical and Pharmaceutical University Sasaki

messages.author: Dr. Anselm Horn
messages.body:
Dear Amber users,
(apologies for cross posting!)
with the beginning of 2021, eight National High Performance Computing
(NHR) Centers have been established throughout Germany.
The three centers in Paderborn, Erlangen, and Berlin have a joint focus
on atomistic simulations and as such form the virtual Atomistic
Simulation Center (ASC).
To celebrate this, we are holding a symposium on atomistic simulations
with a selection of exciting talks from speakers across all areas of
atomistic simulations.
You are cordially invited to the inauguration symposium of our Atomistic
Simulation Center, taking place *online* on October 26-27 2021 (free of
charge, but registration is required).
Further information can be found here:
https://www.tiny.cc/ASC-NHR-2021
Please feel free to forward this invitation to others interested in
atomistic simulations.
Best regards,
Anselm Horn
PD Dr.rer.nat.
Bioinformatik | NHR.FAU
Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg
Germany

messages.author: David A Case
messages.body:
On Mon, Oct 04, 2021, Shiho Ohno wrote:
>
>Q.I'm trying to install AmberTools19 on Amber18.
>
>Initially, I found benchmarks, src, test, and README in the Amber18
>directory, and saved AmberTools19.tar.bz2 in the Amber18 directory
>similarly, and unzipped it using tar xvfj AmberTools19.tar.bz2.
>As a result, a new amber18 directory is added in the amber18 directory
>(there are dat, doc and test directories in the new amber18). Is this normal
>behavior?
THe above is wrong: you need to untar the AmberTools19.tar.bz2 from the
folder *above* the amber18 folder, so that its contents go into the existing
amber18 folder. You don't want two "amber18" folders.
....dac
